title: Operator reconcile: adaptive runtime API draft
content:
Goal
------
Sketch an operator-facing reconcile API for the adaptive runtime manager. Primary use cases: remote operators (SRE, platform), automated controllers (k8s operator-like), and an internal autoscaler that needs to drive desired state for model variants, KV cache population, and batching policies.

Constraints and non-goals
- Non-goal: implement a full k8s API server. Keep lightweight HTTP/WS + idempotent reconcile semantics.
- Constraint: must be tolerant of intermittent connectivity. Client may send a desired state snapshot; server returns a reconciliation token and a best-effort plan.

High-level control loop (notes)
1) Operator / controller posts a desired state document for a tenant/instance.
2) Server validates and computes a diff vs observed state.
3) Server returns an op token and an action list.
4) Client can poll action/step status or open a websocket to stream state transitions.
5) Reconcile is repeated until observed == desired or operator overrides.

API surface (rough)
- POST /v1/operator/reconcile\  (submit desired state)
- GET /v1/operator/reconcile/{token}\  (fetch reconciliation status)
- WS  /v1/operator/events?token={token}\  (stream diffs/events)
- POST /v1/operator/abort/{token}\  (request safe abort)

Example: desired document (payload sketch)
{
  \"tenant_id\": \"acme-inc\",
  \"instance_id\": \"zone-a-1\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-18T16:20:00Z\",
  \"desired\": {
    \"route\": \"/chat/generator\",
    \"model_variant\": \"redwood-3b-q4\",
    \"replicas\": 3,
    \"batching\": { \"max_tokens\": 2048, \"continuous\": true },
    \"kv_prefetch\": { \"anchors\": [\"user_history\", \"session_memo\"], \"prefetch_level\": \"partial\" }
  },
  \"policies\": {
    \"fallback_order\": [\"redwood-3b-q4\", \"redwood-3b-q8\", \"redwood-1b\"],
    \"slo\": { \"p95_ms\": 200 },
    \"merge_strategy\": \"prefer-hosted\"
  }
}

Behavioral guarantees we want
- Idempotency: resubmitting same desired should be a no-op (returns current token + status).
- Causal diffs: server computes minimal action set (scale up/down, warm KV keys, change kernel set).
- Best-effort eventual convergence with observable progress events.

Response sketch
{
  \"token\": \"recon-AQ3f9k\",
  \"accepted_at\": \"2026-02-18T16:20:02Z\",
  \"phase\": \"planning\",
  \"plan\": [
    { \"action\": \"scale_up\", \"target\": 3, \"resource\": \"replica-group-17\" },
    { \"action\": \"warm_kv\", \"anchors\": [\"user_history\"], \"priority\": \"high\" }
  ],
  \"hints\": { \"estimated_completion_sec\": 18 }
}

Event stream (WS) prototype messages
- event.type: planning|apply|progress|complete|error
- event.seq: monotonic int
- payload varies per event.type

ASCII sequence diagram (very rough)
Operator -> POST /reconcile: desired
Server -> Operator: 202 + token
Operator -> WS connect: token
Server -> Operator: event(plan) -> event(apply: scale_up start) -> event(progress: 30%) -> event(complete)

Conflict, merge, and stale handling
- If multiple operators submit conflicting desired states, server assigns them monotonic versions and computes a merge. Merge rule proposals: 
  - owner-priority: last-writer with explicit owner wins unless protected flag set
  - additive: if desired only contains deltas (replicas:+1), sum deltas and cap with max replica policy
- Stale detection: token includes server observed_version. If operator submits an older observed_version, server returns 409 + minimal diff and asks for explicit force flag.

Backoff and safety controls
- Reconcile requests should accept hints: \"safety_window_ms\": 60000 to indicate changes should be staged (no >1 replica changes per minute).
- Server may return staged plan with phases and inter-phase waits.

Authorization and audit
- Calls must be authenticated via mutual TLS or bearer token scoped to tenant.
- Reconcile responses include an audit_id string to cross-reference logs.

Config knobs exposed in payload (draft list)
- reconcile_interval_ms: how often operator expects status updates
- prefer_warm_kv: boolean
- max_concurrent_scale: integer
- prefer_quant_profiles: [\"q4\", \"q8\"]

Open design questions / TODOs
- How tightly do we couple plan execution to infra autoscaler? (operator should be able to opt-out).
- Do we support server-side optimistic execution (server auto-applies low-risk actions) vs purely declarative? Defaults?
- Telemetry contract: include token-level cost estimates per action? (useful for automated cost-aware controllers)
- WS vs long-poll trade-offs for high-frequency updates (we currently lean WS for operator debug).

Safety playbook (abort/rollback)
- Abort semantics: POST /abort/{token} returns current snapshot + rollback plan. Abort returns 202 and begins safe unwind.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rates, SLO breach (p50/p95 skew), or explicit operator abort.

Implementation notes for runtime team
- Keep reconcile handlers idempotent and attach per-action idempotency tokens.
- Store desired documents in a compact change-log (append-only) with TTL for completed tokens.
- Prefer eventual consistent observed state ingestion: actions may be applied out of order; server must be tolerant.

Quick prototype checklist
- [ ] Minimal POST/GET endpoints + in-memory planner (write tests)
- [ ] WS event prototype (stream plan + progress)
- [ ] Audit linkage to telemetry pipeline (audit_id)
- [ ] Simple merge strategy: last-writer-wins but with protected flags

Notes to self
- Keep payloads small: avoid shipping full model graphs in desired — only references (model ids, variant tags).
- Make sure plan objects include \"estimated_cost_units\" so Optimize tooling can pick up and compare plans.

References
- ENG-3789 (controller prototypes)
- runtime PR 942 (plan serialization sketch)

End of draft.
